title: Build Settings & Target Platforms
description: Explore the Build Settings window, switch target platforms, and add scenes to your build list.

slides.title: From Editor to Player 🚀
slides.content:
# What is Building?

**Building** is the process of converting your Unity project into a runnable application for a specific platform (Windows, Android, iOS, Web, etc.).

You configure everything in **File → Build Settings**. This window lists all your scenes, allows you to choose a target platform, and set global build options.

Think of it as the final export command that packages your game for distribution.

quizData.question: Which menu opens the Build Settings window?
quizData.explanation: File → Build Settings is the entry point for building your game.

slides.title: Scenes in Build 📄
slides.content:
# Which Scenes to Include

The top section lists all scenes currently added to the build. Only scenes checked will be included.

- Drag scenes from the Project window into the list.
- The first scene (index 0) is the one that loads when the application starts.
- You can reorder scenes by dragging.

Make sure all necessary scenes are present, otherwise you'll get errors at runtime when trying to load them.

quizData.question: Which scene in the Build Settings list loads first when the game starts?

options.text: The one with the smallest index
The one at the top of the Hierarchy

quizData.explanation: Scene index 0 is the initial scene.

slides.title: Platform Selection 🖥️📱
slides.content:
# Changing the Target

At the bottom, you see the current **Platform**. Unity displays all supported platforms:
- PC, Mac & Linux Standalone
- iOS, Android
- WebGL
- Universal Windows Platform (UWP)
- PS4, PS5, Xbox, Switch (require developer account)

To switch, select the platform and click **Switch Platform**. Unity will re‑import assets for that platform (takes time).

You can also install platform support modules if missing via Unity Hub → Installs → Add Modules.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Install Modules Early

Make sure you installed the necessary build support modules when you set up your Unity Editor. Without them, the platform option will show a download icon.
